title: fix(metadata): revertPackage finds a code-shipped package's members by the _packageId stamp
body:
Part of #22113. This PR delivers the revert half. Two decisions stay with the card (see "Open decisions" below), so merging it must not close the card.

Clause-②: no

## What changes

`MetadataManager.revertPackage` now finds a package's members through one private helper, `collectPackageMembers`. The helper reads three keys: `packageId`, `package`, and the private `_packageId` stamp. The stamp has two producers:

- the metadata plugin's artifact loader, through `applyProtection` (ADR-0010 §3.7);
- the ObjectQL object bridge, which copies `SchemaRegistry.getAllObjects()`'s owner tag onto every object it registers in the metadata service.

A code-shipped item carries only the stamp. The stamp is also the key the metadata protocol uses to scope this registry's items when it serves a package's reads.

With the members found, the existing per-item branches answer. A code-shipped package that nothing was ever published for gets the declared `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` "Package '…' has never been published" instead of `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` "No metadata items found". A published package is restored exactly as before. An id that nothing carries still answers 404.

## Why `publishPackage` and `revertPackage` now read different key sets

The ruling routes both methods through one helper that also reads the stamp. Commit `0edb299` did that. Then I measured it at the door, and commit `cffca05` took the stamp back out of `publishPackage` only. The helper is unchanged and `revertPackage` still uses it, with all three keys. `publishPackage` keeps its original inline two-key lookup, with a comment saying why.

Measured on an `objectstack dev --fresh` boot of `examples/app-showcase`. Base is `51290bc`; "helper in both" is `0edb299`, built and booted:

| `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish` | base | helper in both methods |
|---|---|---|
| `com.objectstack.platform-objects` | 200, `success: false`, "No metadata items found" | 200, `success: true`, `itemsPublished: 3`, `version: 1` |
| `com.objectstack.service.job` | 200, `success: false`, "No metadata items found" | 200, `success: true`, `itemsPublished: 2`, `version: 1` |
| `com.example.showcase` | 200, `success: true`, `itemsPublished: 2` (its two authored-`packageId` capabilities) | 200, `success: false`: 7 validation errors (6 aggregated view containers "must have a name field", 1 api namespace gate) |
| `com.objectstack.setup` | 200, `success: false`, "No metadata items found" | unchanged |

With the stamp read, nothing in `publishPackage` refuses a read-only code package (ADR-0070 D2). After the platform-objects publish, `GET /api/v1/meta/object?package=com.objectstack.platform-objects` served `publishedDefinition`, `state`, `version` and `publishedAt` on all three objects. A later revert of that package answered 200 and added a nested `metadata` key holding a copy of each object. Those are writes into a read-only code package that every object read then serves, and at base they could not happen. The ruling itself rejects a silent no-op success on D2 grounds, so a silent real write was not an answer I could ship. Choosing the answer is a decision (Open decision 1 below), so `publishPackage` keeps the base behaviour until it is made.

## Measured at the door: revert, base vs this PR

Same boot, every package `GET /api/v1/packages` lists (26):

| packages | base `51290bc` | this PR (helper in `revertPackage`) |
|---|---|---|
| 18 code-shipped packages that ship objects (`com.objectstack.platform-objects`, `…metadata-objects`, `…service.job`, `…plugin-auth`, …) | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` "No metadata items found" | 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` "has never been published" |
| `com.example.showcase` | 409 | 409 |
| `com.objectstack.setup`, `…account`, `…service-datasource.nav`, the three `…cloud-connection.*-ui`, `…mcp.connect-agent-ui` | 404 | 404 (not fixed here, Open decision 2) |

The revert numbers were read on the `0edb299` build. Its `revertPackage` and helper code are the same as this PR's; only their comments differ.

## What this PR does not fix: `com.objectstack.setup` (the ruling's first pin)

This is measured. The ruling's mechanism does not reach setup. `com.objectstack.setup` registers through the `manifest` service (`SetupAppPlugin.start`, then `manifest.register`, then `ql.registerApp`), so its app, navigation and docs live only in ObjectQL's SchemaRegistry. The metadata service never holds them. The ObjectQL bridge copies objects only, and setup ships none. So `MetadataManager` has no item for setup under any key: with the helper in place, the door still answers 404 for setup and the six other packages above that ship no objects. `GET /api/v1/meta/app?package=com.objectstack.setup` serves the app from the SchemaRegistry. No `MetadataManager` change can satisfy that pin.

## Pins

- `packages/metadata/src/metadata-service.test.ts`, unit:
  - a stamped-only package, never published, answers 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with the exact sentence;
  - membership is any of `packageId`, `package` or `_packageId`, and each member with a snapshot is restored, with a different package's stamped item as the control;
  - `publishPackage` does not publish a stamped-only item, and nothing is snapshotted.
- `packages/runtime/src/package-revert-code-shipped-members.integration.test.ts`, door. It uses a real ObjectQL over better-sqlite3, the real protocol, the real `MetadataManager` and `HttpDispatcher`, and the real producers of the stamp (`getAllObjects()` then `register`, as the bridge does, and `applyProtection`):
  - bridge-stamped objects answer 409, was 404;
  - an `applyProtection`-stamped artifact item answers 409, was 404;
  - control: an unknown id answers 404;
  - control: an authored-`packageId` package publishes, is edited and reverts with 200;
  - control: the publish door does not publish a bridge-stamped package.
- The sibling `package-revert-stored-members.integration.test.ts` (8 tests) stays green.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata test`: 58 files, 870 tests passed. Both ran at `60ed94f`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`, which runs `tsc --noEmit` and then `check:test-typecheck`: exit 0, debt ledger held at 27 files / 190 errors / 68 signatures. Ran at `60ed94f`.
- Door suites, after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata build` (runtime tests resolve `@objectstack/metadata` through `dist/`): 2 files, 14 tests passed. Ran at `cffca05`. The only later commit adds the changeset.
- Ablation. The ` || meta?._packageId === packageId` term was deleted through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hits 1 then 0, blob `0a20c7d` to `c450d1a`). Metadata was rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` confirmed the term was gone from all 36 dist files.
  - Unit: the 2 new revert pins went red, 4 others passed.
  - Door: the 2 new 409 pins went red ("expected 404 to be 409"), the 3 controls stayed green.
  - Restore leg: the blob matched HEAD and `git diff HEAD` was empty. After a rebuild, the preflight found the marker in 4 dist files and the tree clean against HEAD, and the door suite went back to 5 of 5.
- Derived gates. `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `60ed94f` derived 63 families, and all 63 exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a derived zero, since every line recorded its exit code).
- Lint, narrowed and proven: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 3 touched `.ts` files found 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` anywhere), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Open decisions (the card stays open for these)

1. **How should the publish door answer a read-only code package once `publishPackage` finds its stamped members?** This is the ruling's second pin. Options:
   - (A) `publishPackage` takes the helper, and the door refuses a non-writable package first with the existing `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` (`requireWritablePackage`, as `disable` and `delete` already do).
   - (B) Keep the two keys. This is what the PR ships.
   - (C) Take the helper with no guard. The measured result is in the table above.
2. **Packages whose items the metadata service never holds** (setup and six others). Options:
   - (A) After the metadata service answers "no members", the revert door asks the ObjectQL registry and answers the ruled 409 for a package it knows.
   - (B) The revert door refuses a non-writable package with 422 after the protocol's stored answer. This re-rules 409 to 422.
   - (C) Leave the 404.

The four-axis analysis is in the dev report on the card.

## Acceptance notes

- `MetadataManager.unregisterPackage` still matches on `packageId` and `package` only. It has no production caller in this repository, so I left it as it was.
- `MetadataManager.query({ packageId })` filters on `packageId` alone. This is a separate reader, not touched.
- Before this PR, publishing then reverting a flat (non-envelope) item adds a nested `metadata` key holding a copy of the item, because revert writes `metadata: publishedDefinition` and publish snapshots the whole flat item. The only measured way to reach it is the "helper in both" build above, so no card is filed.
- M4 (the contract-review case from #22090: a code package, published, with an organization overlay draft). The door returns at the protocol's stored answer before `revertPackage` is called, so this PR cannot change that answer. Checked by reading the door, not measured.
